test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper sells a pair of shoes at a discount of 34% and still makes a profit of 10%. If the cost price of the pair of shoes is ₹480, find its marked price.
solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 34%

Profit = 10%

Cost Price (CP) = ₹480

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit%)

SP = Marked Price (MP) × (1 - Discount%)

**Calculation:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit%)

SP = 480 × (1 + 0.10)

⇒ SP = 480 × 1.10

⇒ SP = ₹528

SP = Marked Price (MP) × (1 - Discount%)

528 = MP × (1 - 0.34)

⇒ 528 = MP × 0.66

⇒ MP = 528 / 0.66

⇒ MP = ₹800

**The marked price of the shoes is ₹800.**
